anchor.note: English is the comparison anchor because ordinary English nouns do not belong to grammatical masculine/feminine/neuter classes, even though pronouns can encode gender.

scope_note: How languages classify nouns and trigger agreement. Article examples are illustrative only. A language may have grammatical gender without articles, multiple article allomorphs within one gender, no grammatical noun gender, or a broader noun-class system.

rules.summary_en: Ordinary English nouns are not assigned grammatical masculine, feminine, or neuter classes, and the definite article the does not change for noun gender.
tips_en: Do not confuse gendered pronouns such as he and she with a grammatical gender class on every noun.
English is useful as a zero-gender comparison, not as a universal default.

languages.notes: English retains limited natural-gender distinctions in pronouns and some lexical pairs; that is different from a grammatical noun-gender agreement system.

rules.summary_en: Masculine nouns take masculine agreement, including el/un in the singular and los/unos in the plural, plus masculine forms of adjectives that vary for gender.
tips_en: Learn a new noun with an article: el libro, el problema.
Many nouns ending in -o are masculine, but the ending is a clue rather than a guarantee.

rules.summary_en: Feminine nouns take feminine agreement, including la/una in the singular and las/unas in the plural, plus feminine forms of adjectives that vary for gender.
tips_en: Learn a new noun with an article: la casa, la mano.
Many nouns ending in -a are feminine, but exceptions are normal.

rules.summary_en: Word endings often give useful gender clues, but Spanish noun gender is lexical and cannot be determined from -o/-a alone.
tips_en: Use endings as a prediction, then confirm with the noun’s article or dictionary entry.
Memorize exceptions as whole noun phrases: la mano, el día, el mapa, el problema.

rules.summary_en: Neuter lo can nominalize a quality or idea, as in lo importante, but it is not an article for ordinary neuter nouns.
tips_en: If an ordinary noun follows, lo is not the normal article to choose.
Think of lo + adjective as an abstract quality or aspect, not as a third noun class.

rules.summary_en: Esto, eso, and aquello are neuter demonstratives used for unspecified things, situations, or ideas and do not directly modify ordinary nouns.
tips_en: Use este/esta + noun when the noun is stated and has grammatical gender.
Use esto/eso/aquello when you are pointing to an unspecified thing or whole idea.

languages.notes: Spanish has two grammatical genders for ordinary nouns. Neuter lo/esto/eso/aquello are real neuter forms but do not establish a third ordinary noun gender.
